questions.question: For real $A$ ($m\times n$) and $G$ ($n\times m$) consider (1) $AGA=A$, (2) $GAG=G$, (3) $AG$ symmetric, (4) $GA$ symmetric. Which conditions define $G$ as the Moore-Penrose inverse $A^+$?
Let $A$ be a real $m\times n$ matrix, possibly non-square and rank-deficient. How many $n\times m$ matrices satisfy all four Penrose conditions for $A$?
options: Exactly one if $A$ has full rank, none otherwise
Exactly one if $m=n$, none if $m\neq n$

questions.question: Let $A$ be a real $m\times n$ matrix with Moore-Penrose inverse $A^+$. Which statement about $AA^+$ is true?
options: It projects orthogonally onto the row space $\operatorname{Row}(A)$
Its range is the null space $\operatorname{Null}(A^{\top})$
It is the orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{Col}(A)$

questions.question: View a real number $a$ as a $1\times1$ matrix. What is its Moore-Penrose inverse $a^+$?
Let $A$ be a real $m\times n$ matrix and $\boldsymbol{y}\in \operatorname{Null}(A^{\top})$, i.e. $\boldsymbol{y}$ is orthogonal to every column of $A$. What is $A^+\boldsymbol{y}$?
What is the Moore-Penrose inverse of $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$?
options: It does not exist, as $A$ is singular

questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{a}=(0,3,4)^{\top}$, a $3\times1$ matrix of full column rank. What is $\boldsymbol{a}^+=(\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{a})^{-1}\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}$?
Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}$ and $G=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$. Which of the Penrose conditions (1) $AGA=A$, (2) $GAG=G$, (3) $AG$ symmetric, (4) $GA$ symmetric fail?
options: Only (2) fails; the other three hold

questions.question: Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&3\end{pmatrix}$, so $A^+=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&\tfrac{1}{3}\end{pmatrix}$, and $\boldsymbol{b}=(4,6)^{\top}$. What is $\boldsymbol{x}=A^+\boldsymbol{b}$, the least-squares solution of $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ of minimum norm?
options: None, since the system is inconsistent

questions.question: Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}=5\boldsymbol{w}\boldsymbol{w}^{\top}$ with the unit vector $\boldsymbol{w}=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}}(1,2)^{\top}$, so its only positive singular value is $5$. What is $A^+$?
Which identity holds for every real $m\times n$ matrix $A$ (and, where it appears, every real $n\times p$ matrix $B$ and real $c\neq0$)?
For $\varepsilon\neq0$ let $A_\varepsilon=\operatorname{diag}(1,\varepsilon)$. Which statement about $A_\varepsilon^+$ as $\varepsilon\to0$ is correct?
options: $A_\varepsilon^+$ stays bounded, since all its entries are at most $1$

questions.question: Let $A$ be a real $m\times n$ matrix with full column rank and $m>n$, so $A^+=(A^{\top}A)^{-1}A^{\top}$. Which statement is true?
Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&2\\0&0\end{pmatrix}=U\Sigma V^{\top}$ with $U=I_2$, $\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(2,0)$ and $V=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$. What is $A^+$?
Let $\boldsymbol{a}=(1,-1)^{\top}$, a $2\times1$ matrix, so $\boldsymbol{a}^+=\tfrac{1}{2}(1,-1)$. What are $\boldsymbol{a}\boldsymbol{a}^+$ and $\boldsymbol{a}^+\boldsymbol{a}$?
The single equation $x_1+2x_2=5$ is written as $A\boldsymbol{x}=b$ with $A=(1,2)$ and $b=5$, so $A^+=\tfrac{1}{5}(1,2)^{\top}$. Which solution is $A^+b$?
Let $A$ be a real $m\times n$ matrix and $G=A^+$, so that (1) $AGA=A$, (2) $GAG=G$, (3) $AG$ symmetric, (4) $GA$ symmetric. What is the Moore-Penrose inverse $G^+$ of the $n\times m$ matrix $G$?
options: $A$: swapping the roles of $A$ and $G$ turns (1) into (2) and (3) into (4)
$A^{\top}$: inverting twice returns a transpose, as $G$ has the shape of $A^{\top}$
$A$ only when $A$ is invertible; otherwise $G^+$ differs from $A$
Not unique: every generalized inverse of $G$ qualifies, $A$ among them

questions.question: Let $G$ satisfy $AGA=A$ for a real matrix $A$, with $\operatorname{rank}G>\operatorname{rank}A$. Can $G$ be the Moore-Penrose inverse $A^+$?
options: Yes; rank plays no role in the Penrose conditions
No, because $A^+$ always has full rank

questions.question: Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$. Which matrix is $A^+$?
Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&1\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix}$, a $2\times3$ matrix of full row rank. Which $3\times2$ matrix is its Moore-Penrose inverse $A^+$?
